messages:
Maria: heads up — ran the pagination stress in the Go sample app against Dedicated and we saw a big burst of 429s after about 120s. seems linked to retries + page token logic. :frowning:

Ajay: thanks. any logs or a repro script? is this the new sampleapp using the go-sdk v0.9.x?

Maria: yes v0.9.4. repro steps in the test harness: request pages concurrently (concurrency=8), when a page fails we retry the single page, but the harness shows the client re-firing pending page requests in a tight loop. attaching snippet of the client loop:

Maria: ```go
// simplified loop
for i := 0; i < pages; i++ {
  go func(p int){
    resp, err := client.List(ctx, &ListReq{PageToken: token})
    if err != nil {
      // naive retry
      resp, err = client.List(ctx, &ListReq{PageToken: token})
    }
    // process
  }(i)
}
```

Ajay: uh that's the thing — the Go SDK sample didn't include the internal concurrency limiter that JS added last quarter. JS has a request queue + backoff with jitter. Go right now just relies on caller-level control.

Thomas: SRE note — Dedicated enforces soft QPS smoothing per-customer and then clips to hard quotas. If clients hammer after a transient, we see cascades. The alert triggered: `quota.exceeded.dedicated-prod` around 1769123449.

sre-bot: ALERT: quota.exceeded.dedicated-prod for customer:redwood-dev-samples — 429 spike (30s avg qps 2.3x threshold)

Ken (QA): I reproduced locally. Script: `go run ./stress -concurrency 8 -pages 200 -retry=1` -> 429s start at ~95s. I tried increasing retry delay and that mitigates but the default sample is too aggressive.

Ajay: okay. two things: (1) fix sample app to show proper concurrency/backpressure primitives, (2) patch the Go SDK to provide an opt-in limiter (same semantics as JS) so users can enable smoothing without reimplementing.

Maria: agree. we should also add a CI test that fails if the sample causes >10% 429s in the harness.

Ajay: implementation sketch: add a TokenBucket with capacity = 50 reqs/sec and a per-call permit wait with exponential jitter. fallback path is immediate when user sets `DisableSmoothing=true`. Pseudocode:

Ajay: ```go
lim := NewSmoother(permPerSec:50)
lim.Acquire(ctx) // waits + jitter
resp, err := client.List(ctx, req)
```

Thomas: can we avoid introducing blocking in hot paths? prefer non-blocking queue with drop or backpressure signal. but token bucket is fine if the Acquire has a short timeout.

Ken (QA): I'll add an e2e that runs against a staging Dedicated and asserts retries + smoothing keep 429s < 5% at the same load.

Elaine: from product: we need to be careful about changing defaults — many users rely on raw low-latency behavior. Make smoothing opt-in for 0.9.8, but plan default-on for 1.0 after rollout and docs.

Ajay: plan sounds good. I'll open a PR with the sample app change + a new `smoothing` package. Will add feature flag env var `RW_GO_SMOOTHING=on|off`.

Maria: timeline? can we get a patch this week?

Ajay: I can do a draft today, code + unit tests tomorrow, QA e2e by Friday. tagging @Ken (QA) for e2e validation.

Ken (QA): ack. will provision a staging Dedicated run and attach results.

Thomas: SRE — we'll suppress noisy alerts for the sample customer during the canary window. please coordinate times.

Maria: cool. one more ask — can we add a tiny doc blurb in onboarding that says "Go sample does not auto-throttle by default" to reduce friction for new users hitting 429s in tutorials?

Elaine: yes, we'll update the quickstart and include recommended env flags.

Ajay: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/420 (draft). includes: sample fix, smoothing pkg (opt-in), unit tests, docs.

Maria: perfect. thanks team. i'll follow up with a short postmortem note after QA results. :thumbsup:
